text: California's all-cause unplanned 30-day readmission rate was 15.95% in 2024 (ICD-10), up 0.99 percentage points from 2023 and +1.47 pp since 2016, the first ICD-10 year (14.48%).
By expected payer (2024), the highest rate was MediCare (17.02%) and the lowest Self-Pay (6.98%). These are descriptive associations, not causal effects.
By age group (2024), the highest rate was 45 to 64 years (16.44%) and the lowest 18 to 44 years (13.47%); 65 years and above was 16.36%.
Among 50 counties with at least 1,000 admissions in 2024, rates ranged from 10.19% (Siskiyou) to 18.78% (Butte).
Statewide isolated CABG 30-day readmission moved from 12.15% (2018-2019) to 11.16% (2022-2023).

On the held-out 2022-2023 window (n=118 hospitals), Linear Regression (MAE 2.54 pp) is statistically indistinguishable from the persistence baseline (MAE 2.49 pp); bootstrap 95% CI of the MAE difference [-0.23, +0.34] pp. Random Forest MAE was 2.74 pp.

Rolling two-year windows share a calendar year, which inflates persistence. When input and target windows do not overlap, persistence MAE rises to 3.96 pp while Linear Regression reaches 3.52 pp (better in 88% of grouped-CV folds).
Permutation importance: 'prev_readmit_rate' dominates (MAE +1.76 pp when shuffled); previous post-operative stroke rate and case volume add little predictive signal.
Statewide ischemic stroke 30-day readmission (risk-adjusted) went from 12.80% (2011-2012) to 11.80% (2014-2015).
Statewide ischemic stroke 30-day mortality (risk-adjusted) went from 10.55% (2011-2012) to 9.81% (2014-2015).

Hospital-level stroke readmission and mortality rates are nearly uncorrelated (Pearson r between -0.12 and +0.05 across periods): a hospital's mortality performance says little about its readmission performance.

Stroke model on the 2014-2015 hold-out (n=259): Linear Regression MAE 1.85 pp vs persistence 1.98 pp (-6.4%). Bootstrap 95% CI of the MAE difference [-0.27, +0.01] pp: the difference is not statistically reliable at the 95% level (the interval includes zero), although Linear Regression had lower error in 97% of bootstrap resamples.
